title: Ebola Virus Sequencing Protocol
author: Josh Quick
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7nwhmfe
materials: In the mastermix hood set up the multiplex PCR reactions as follows in 0.2mL 8-strip PCR tubes: Component Pool 1 Pool 2 NEB Q5 Polymerase 2X MasterMix 12.5 µL 12.5 µL Primer Pool 1 or 2 (10µM) 3.8 µL 4.0 µL Water 6.2 µL 6.0 µL Total 22.5 µL 22.5 µL The mastermix hood should prepared by sterilising with UV and treated with MediPal wipes, DNAway and RNAseZap reagents. Wipe down the hood with each sequentially, allowing 5 minutes for drying between each. Pipettes should also be treated in the same way, and UV treated for 30 mins between library preparations. This step should be carried out in the mastermix hood and template should not be taken anywhere near the mastermix hood at any stage.

steps.title: Dilute RNA based on Ct
steps.instruction: If the clinical sample Ct is 12‑15 dilute the RNA 1:100 in water; if Ct is 15‑18 dilute 1:10; if Ct is 18‑35 use undiluted RNA. Use 10 µL of the (diluted or undiluted) RNA as template.

steps.title: Prepare annealing mix
steps.instruction: In a 0.2 mL 8‑strip tube combine 1 µL 50 µM random hexamers, 1 µL 10 mM dNTP mix (10 mM each), and 10 µL template RNA (total 12 µL). Gently mix by pipetting and pulse‑spin to collect liquid at the bottom.

steps.title: Anneal RNA
steps.instruction: Incubate the annealing mix at 65 °C for 5 min, then place on ice for 1 min. Gently mix by pipetting and pulse‑spin.

steps.title: Add reverse transcription reagents
steps.instruction: Add to the annealed template: 4 µL 100 mM DTT, 1 µL SSIV Buffer, 1 µL RNaseOUT (RNase inhibitor), and 1 µL SuperScript IV Reverse Transcriptase (total reaction volume 20 µL). Gently mix by pipetting and pulse‑spin.

steps.title: Reverse transcription incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate at 42 °C for 1 h 30 min, then at 70 °C for 10 min. Hold at 5 °C until further use.

steps.title: Prepare primer pools
steps.instruction: If required, resuspend lyophilised primers to 100 µM each. In a sterile PCR cabinet, add 5 µL of each primer pair to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube labelled “Pool 1 (100 µM)” or “Pool 2 (100 µM)”. Bring volumes to 505 µL for Pool 1 and 530 µL for Pool 2 (these are the 100 µM stock pools). Dilute each pool 1:10 with molecular‑grade water to obtain 10 µM primer stocks and aliquot; keep primers away from any template until cDNA addition.

steps.title: Sterilise PCR hood
steps.instruction: UV‑treat the template hood, then sequentially wipe with MediPal, DNAway, and RNaseZap wipes, allowing 5 min drying between each wipe. UV‑treat pipettes for 30 min between library preparations.

steps.title: Assemble PCR reactions
steps.instruction: In the sterilised hood add 2.5 µL cDNA to each PCR tube. Add 3.8 µL of Pool 1 (10 µM) and 4.0 µL of Pool 2 (10 µM) to achieve a final primer concentration of 0.015 µM per primer in a 25 µL reaction. Mix well by pipetting and pulse‑centrifuge to collect the liquid at the bottom.

steps.title: Run PCR thermal program
steps.instruction: Program the thermal cycler: 98 °C for 30 s (heat activation); then 25‑35 cycles of 98 °C for 15 s (denaturation), 65 °C for 5 min (annealing/extension); hold at 4 °C indefinitely. Use 25 cycles for Ct 18‑21 and up to 35 cycles for Ct 35.

steps.title: Pool PCR products
steps.instruction: Combine the entire contents of the Pool 1 and Pool 2 PCR reactions for each biological sample into a single 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Clean up amplicons with SPRI beads
steps.instruction: Perform amplicon clean‑up using SPRI beads following Josh Quick’s SPRI‑bead cleanup protocol.

steps.title: Quantify amplicon pools
steps.instruction: Measure the concentration of each pooled amplicon using a Quantus Fluorometer with the ONE dsDNA assay.

steps.title: Normalize amplicon input
steps.instruction: Add 10 ng of each amplicon pool to a tube and dilute to a final volume of 10 µL (1 ng/µL). Note that 6 samples are required per native‑barcoded library to obtain sufficient material.

steps.title: Native barcode ligation
steps.instruction: Perform one‑pot native barcoding of the normalized amplicons using the Ultra II ligation module (compatible with the Ultra II end‑repair/dA‑tailing module) according to the kit instructions.

steps.title: Quantify final library
steps.instruction: Quantify the ligated library with a Quantus Fluorometer using the ONE dsDNA assay. The final library can be stored in EB at 4 °C for up to one week, or proceed directly to sequencing.

steps.title: Prime flowcell and load library
steps.instruction: Prime the MinION flowcell and load 30 ng of the sequencing library (optimal loading amount for short amplicons).

steps.title: Start MinION sequencing run
steps.instruction: Launch the sequencing run using MinKNOW software.
